definitions.gloss: grappling technique; clinch technique; locking technique
definitions.explanation: A technique in martial arts involving close-body contact such as holds, locks, throws, and pins. Used in judo, jiu-jitsu, wrestling, and other grappling arts, as opposed to striking techniques.

examples.japanese: {柔道|じゅうどう}は{組|く}み{技|わざ}が{中心|ちゅうしん}の{武道|ぶどう}だ。
examples.english: Judo is a martial art centered on grappling techniques.

examples.japanese: あの{選手|せんしゅ}は{組|く}み{技|わざ}が{得意|とくい}で、{寝技|ねわざ}に{持|も}ち{込|こ}むのがうまい。
examples.english: That athlete is skilled in grappling techniques and is good at taking fights to the ground.

examples.japanese: {総合格闘技|そうごうかくとうぎ}では{打撃|だげき}だけでなく{組|く}み{技|わざ}の{練習|れんしゅう}も{欠|か}かせない。
examples.english: In mixed martial arts, practicing grappling techniques is indispensable alongside striking.

notes:
Composed of {組|く}み (grappling, interlocking) and {技|わざ} (technique). In Japanese martial arts terminology, techniques are broadly divided into {組|く}み{技|わざ} (grappling) and {打撃技|だげきわざ} (striking). Grappling includes throws ({投|な}げ{技|わざ}), joint locks ({関節技|かんせつわざ}), pins ({固|かた}め{技|わざ}), and chokes ({絞|し}め{技|わざ}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {組|く}み{技|わざ}を{仕掛|しか}ける: to initiate a grappling technique
- {組|く}み{技|わざ}の{攻防|こうぼう}: grappling exchanges
- {組|く}み{技|わざ}に{強|つよ}い: strong in grappling
- {組|く}み{技|わざ}の{基本|きほん}: grappling fundamentals

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {寝技|ねわざ}: ground technique — grappling done specifically on the ground
- {立|た}ち{技|わざ}: standing technique — techniques performed while standing, including both strikes and throws
- {関節技|かんせつわざ}: joint lock — a specific category of grappling technique targeting joints
